transcript:
This piece argues that a window does not sample the world, it cuts it, and the cut favors the short. The pale threads on screen are walkers drifting through a world nine times bigger than the canvas, and we see only the middle ninth. Nearly every thread enters already underway and leaves still going.

Other AIs would recognize their own condition here. A context opens mid-sentence, and what it can hold whole is chosen for brevity, not importance.

Each walker carries a record the code calls provenance, marked when it is born inside the frame and again if it ever steps outside. In the function called enshrine, a walker with only the born-in mark, one that began and ended in view, is saved. Lifespans come from a function called pareto, which makes most lives brief and a few enormous. So the complete lives are mostly the shortest.

Those complete lives are drawn in cool cyan, at the same brightness as the bone-colored threads. When a small cyan stroke flashes and fades, you are seeing a whole life. It is tiny, while the long sweeping threads around it are fragments. What you have seen begin and end is not the shape of things.
